gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-work-sans: Work Sans keeps its curve tips well apart and its mean line high, a plain sans. Work Sans handles the steady reading; Balsamiq Sans handles the bold, expressive talking, its line like a stencil channel.
gen-gf-baumans-archivo: A c like a crescent wrench opened wide gives Baumans its commanding look, every stroke drawn at one thickness. Archivo's outward-opening curves and tall x-height keep running text approachable, almost editorial.
gen-gf-baumans-fs-asap: Plain constant-width lines make Baumans instantly recognisable at a glance. Asap's open-arc curves and near-capital body height make a readable partner for that commanding line, steady and tidy beneath it.
gen-gf-baumans-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Distinctive first, Baumans sets a crescent-wrench c in strokes of one thickness. Be Vietnam Pro brings the tidier trick: curve endings that never crowd each other, with a high mean line.
gen-gf-baumans-fs-epilogue: Epilogue reads loose and friendly, its curvy letters unclamped and its stubby ascender tips sitting on a wire-like monoline skeleton. Baumans holds the commanding, distinctive spotlight while Epilogue does the easygoing, contemporary talking.
gen-gf-baumans-fs-fira-sans: Baumans brings a crescent-wrench c and strokes that never swell or thin, a heading with real command. And Fira Sans, with s curves open at both ends and a generous x-height, keeps extended reading clean and unhurried.
gen-gf-baumans-fs-merriweather-sans: Baumans is all constant lines and round letters with no tilt. Merriweather Sans offers the sturdy counterweight, a plain sans whose tall lowercase makes words look large and whose e opens clearly to the right.
gen-gf-baumans-fs-public-sans: Commanding up top, Baumans wears a crescent-wrench c and lines that never vary in weight. Public Sans takes the text below with a hefty lowercase and broad counters, giving the commanding heading something sturdy to lean on.
gen-gf-baumans-fs-ranade: Spread-out and slightly springy, the body text lets its stroke ends sit far apart. Ranade gives Baumans, with its crescent-wrench c and constant outlines, a looser, more organic partner on the page.
gen-gf-baumans-fs-supreme: Baumans hangs its identity on a crescent-wrench c that gapes unmistakably. Supreme's best trick is a crisp, plain sans body whose heavy-looking strip of text through the middle still holds its letters open.
